summary: Request: SQL-friendly audit view + identity translation table and resumable export proof for analytics
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a production-ready, SQL-consumable view of audit events (parquet/ndjson -> logical table) with a separate identity_translation table that maps Redwood internal IDs to FinEdge canonical IDs. They also require a resumable incremental export (resume_token / offset proof) and a short proof document showing deterministic ordering and checksum so FinEdge analytics can safely JOIN and backfill without double-counting.

Impact:
- FinEdge data engineering cannot deliver regulatory reporting (transaction traceability) to auditors for March 2026 cut without a reliable SQL-ready export.
- They are blocking a quarterly audit; business impact: critical compliance deadline.

Environment:
- Redwood prod cluster serving FinEdge tenant in us-east, using the tenant-scoped audit pipeline v2.
- Customer uses Snowflake as the downstream consumer and expects a table-like schema (event_ts, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_fingerprint, action, model, request_id, request_payload_hash, resume_token).

Requested deliverable:
1) A sample SQL view definition (DDL or CREATE VIEW) that maps current ndjson audit to a flattened, typed schema that is stable across export runs.
2) A separate identity_translation table with example rows and a short signing/rotation note.
3) A reproducible resume_token format and a worked example showing how to resume from token X and verify no gaps using checksums.
4) Short attestation: ordering guarantees (UTC monotonic event_ts + per-tenant sequence_id) and checksum algorithm used for per-batch manifest.

Attachments from customer:
- Example Snowflake loader SQL (attached in customer email).
- Desired sample rows and column types (provided inline).
steps_to_reproduce: Customer subscribes to audit delta endpoint with parameter format=ndjson and window=hourly
They request first page for timeframe 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-01T01:00:00Z and receive ndjson.gz with events but no resume_token in manifest

Customer attempts to INSERT INTO audit_table SELECT FROM external_stage using manifest, then runs a JOIN to their identity table and finds mismatched actor IDs (redwood_internal_id present, customer_id missing)
Customer asks to re-run the export incrementally starting from their last successfully applied offset; cannot prove deterministic order so they fear duplicates

comments: Priya Kapoor (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: FinEdge provided a Snowflake loader and says auditors expect a canonical CSV/SQL view. Asks for an example DDL and an explanation of resume logic.

Santiago Ruiz (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. I will validate manifest format and produce a sample CREATE VIEW plus identity_translation mapping. Pulling logs and contacting infra for resume_token gap regression.

Eng SRE (Marina Petrov) - 2026-03-11: Noted a recent manifest change in release 4.2 that deprecated resume_token field in favor of per-batch sequence_id ranges. Will confirm compatibility and supply back-compat manifest with resume_token for enterprise tenants.
Customer (FinEdge: DataEng contact - Michael Ong) - 2026-03-11: Appreciates progress; requests that the SQL view include request_payload_hash and a stable event_id usable as a primary key for dedupe.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: release 4.2 made a manifest schema change; enterprise export path should still populate resume_token but it appears empty for this tenant. Action taken: pulled manifests for the tenant (mf-7a9c,mf-7a9d) and validated per-batch sequence_id ranges are present. Sequence_id provides the ordering hook. Next steps: generate a durable resume_token format combining (manifest_id, sequence_id_end, sha256_manifest) and provide a sample verification SQL for Snowflake. Also build identity_translation mapping using lookup table from FinEdge-provided mapping file. Noted potential follow-up: small window where event_ts can be equal across many events; use (event_ts, sequence_id) as deterministic sort key.
resolution: (pending) Santiago to deliver sample SQL view, identity_translation DDL, a resume_token spec, and an attestation note. Temporary workaround: we provided customer with per-batch sequence_id ranges to allow them to do idempotent loads (WHERE sequence_id > last_applied_sequence). Permanent fix: backfill manifest to include resume_token for enterprise customers in next hotfix. See linked PR for manifest shim.
notes_for_followup: Deliverables must include a signed one-page attestation (pdf) for auditors describing ordering and checksum algorithm (sha256) used per batch.
Coordinate with Product Security to confirm identity_translation table PII handling and redaction guidance before shipping mapping sample.
Schedule a 30-min working session with FinEdge DataEng on 2026-03-12 to walk through Snowflake load pattern.
